The House is now sitting. MPs will begin by debating the second reading of the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill.

TW: This briefing contains references to suicide.

The @commonslibrary have published an impartial research briefing to keep MPs informed ahead of tomorrow's debate on the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill.
Read now: commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-10123/?utm_campaign=1124-rice-routine-spotlight&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter&utm_term=hoc

Last week, I held events across Chipping Barnet to listen to our community’s thoughts, experiences, and questions about the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill.

stories.title: What is assisted dying in the UK?
stories.snippet:
The bill would allow mentally competent adults in England and Wales with 
fewer than six months to live to request and receive help to end their 
lives. Assisted suicide is currently illegal in Britain and carries a 
prison sentence of up to 14 years.

stories.title: Is euthanasia legal in the UK?
stories.snippet: Both euthanasia and assisted suicide are illegal under English law.
